Contreras had an RBI single in the first inning, a walk in the sixth inning and another base hit in the eighth inning. Defensively, he caught two runners stealing to end innings and won two ABS challenges. He became the best catcher this century to have multiple caught stealings and hits in a World Series game, per MLB Network's Sarah Langs. Joe Girardi of the New York Yankees was the last player to achiev
item.content:encoded:
William Contreras was undoubtedly the Milwaukee Brewers MVP in Game 1 of the World Series.
Contreras had an RBI single in the first inning, a walk in the sixth inning and another base hit in the eighth inning. Defensively, he caught two runners stealing to end innings and won two ABS challenges.
He became the best catcher this century to have multiple caught stealings and hits in a World Series game, per MLB Network's Sarah Langs. Joe Girardi of the New York Yankees was the last player to achieve that feat.
Girardi did it in Game 3 of the 1999 World Series against the Atlanta Braves. It had been 27 years since a catcher had a game like that, and Contreras seemed due to break the drought.
He was the best catcher in the regular season at catching runners, and the Tampa Bay Rays are a team that likes to run. Something had to give, and it was Contreras who came out on top.
At the plate, he continued a red-hot October, and the Brewers will need him to continue his hitting ways for the rest of the series. The Brewers can go up 2-0 on the Rays on Saturday, and if Contreras is swinging the bat as he has been, there is really no pitcher who is going to give him problems.
The Rays are expected to stay aggressive on the basepaths, so Contreras' arm will continue to be tested. In Game 1, he changed the complexion of the game by erasing baserunners, and could do the same in Game 2.
More MLB: Brewers Pitcher Close To Breaking Andrew Miller's MLB Record

item.content:encoded:
De raíces mexicanas, los peloteros de los Brewers, Joey Ortiz, y JoJo Romero, están ante la oportunidad de ser parte del primer equipo campeón de la Serie Mundial en la historia de la franquicia de Milwaukee.
Romero y Ortiz integraron la Selección Mexicana que compitió en el pasado Clásico Mundial de Beisbol de 2023 y 2026, respectivamente, junto a jugadores como Jonathan Aranda.
Nacido en California, shortstop y tercera base, Joey Ortiz, reconoció el momento que vive Aranda con los Rays y ahora les toca enfrentarlo en el Clásico de Otoño.
“Es un gran jugador, muy profesional, es uno de los mejores bateadores que yo he visto en la liga y será muy divertido competir entre nosotros”, declaró el pelotero de los Brewers.
Jonathan Aranda, el primera base de los Rays y originario de Tijuana, bateó de 3-3 con una base por bolas y una carrera anotada en su debut en un Clásico de Otoño.
El pitcher zurdo, JoJo Romero, dijo que sus abuelos son aficionados de las Chivas, en otro tiempo fanáticos del futbol, pero ahora disfrutan ver el beisbol.
Romero reconoció que fue especial haber sido parte de la Selección Mexicana en el Clásico Mundial de Beisbol celebrado en 2023 con el equipo llegando hasta las semifinales.
“Claro, es grandioso, toda mi familia siempre me ha apoyado, mis abuelos no crecieron viendo béisbol sino soccer, pero ellos disfrutan verme jugar beisbol y por eso siento que también los represento”, declaró el relevista de los Brewers de Milwaukee.
“Ellos hoy en día disfrutan verme por la TV, cuando hablo con ellos se sienten muy orgullosos de lo que he logrado, me enseñaron mucho de lo que es trabajar duro, no parar hasta lograr los objetivos y podré llegar hasta este tipo de momentos”.
Nacido en Camarillo, California, Joseph Abel Romero ha integrado un bullpen que ha contribuido de manera decisiva para que el equipo de Milwaukee esté en el Clásico de Otoño.
Otros peloteros de origen mexicano que han ganado anillo de Serie Mundial son el pitcher Sergio Romo y el catcher, Austin Barnes.

item.title: [House That Hank Built] Matt Olson’s Fielding Bible win puts Braves first baseman in rare company
item.dc:creator: Steven Teal
item.description: Award season is upon us, and the Atlanta Braves have already secured some hardware. It stinks not to see the team in the playoffs, but there were some great performances shown to fans this season. Matt Olson was unsurprisingly among the players who gave fans something to cheer about. His time at the plate was inconsistent at times, but he still put up respectable numbers. item.content:encoded:
Award season is upon us, and the Atlanta Braves have already secured some hardware. It stinks not to see the team in the playoffs, but there were some great performances shown to fans this season. Matt Olson was unsurprisingly among the players who gave fans something to cheer about. His time at the plate was inconsistent at times, but he still put up respectable numbers.
Atlanta's first baseman had a .251/.321/.502 slash line, with 34 doubles, 41 home runs, 93 RBI, and a 122 wRC+. Those are great numbers, but he disappeared in the postseason, which was tough to watch. The offense is one aspect of Olson's impressive game, but his defense remained elite in 2026. His impressive fielding work led to his first award of the season. Olson was awarded a Fielding Bible Award to recognize him as the best defensive first baseman in baseball.
The Fielding Bible Awards are handed out each season to one player at each of the nine positions as the top fielder in MLB at that position. They also award one "multi-position" player, one overall Defensive Player of the Year, and a Defensive Team of the Year. Recipients are voted on by a panel of experts based on a combination of stats, the eye test, and any other factors the voters choose to consider.
Matt Olson's latest defensive honor a reminder of his underrated skill set
Olson was in a tight race with Padres first baseman Ty France this season. However, his incredible OAA and FRV set him apart. He finished the season with an 11 outs above average (OAA) and 12 fielding run value (FRV). Those numbers were both the best in baseball among all first basemen. France edged out Olson in defensive runs saved (DRS), with 15 DRS compared to Olson's 11 DRS.
This win was Olson's sixth Fielding Bible Award at first base, which surpassed Albert Pujols for the most wins at the position. Atlanta's lefty slugger is now tied with Yadier Molina and Andrelton Simmons for the second-most all-time wins among all positions. Olson only trails Mookie Betts, who has seven wins, for the most Fielding Bible Awards.
It likely won't be the last award for Olson, who is also nominated for a Gold Glove Award this season. He continues to be a wonderful addition for the Braves.

item.content:encoded:
Conoce a los peloteros mexicanos que buscan hacer historia en la Serie Mundial de la MLB
Al menos cuatro mexicanos participan en la Serie Mundial de la MLB en este 20226 Joey Ortiz, JoJo Romero, Jonathan Aranda y Manuel Rodríguez.
La Serie Mundial 2026 cuenta con varios mexicanos: Jonathan Aranda, Joey Ortiz y JoJo Romero. Cada uno tiene un papel diferente en sus equipos, pero los tres forman parte de una final que reúne a jugadores vinculados con el beisbol de México.
Los Milwaukee Brewers regresaron a la Serie Mundial después de 44 años. El equipo busca ganar el primer título de su historia con Joey Ortiz en el cuadro interior y JoJo Romero como una de las opciones del bullpen. Por su parte, Jonathan Aranda intenta ayudar a los Tampa Bay Rays a conseguir el campeonato.
Joey Ortiz nació en California y juega como campocorto y tercera base. Durante la temporada regular de 2026, disputó 134 partidos, con un promedio de bateo de .270, nueve jonrones y 47 carreras impulsadas.
La defensa es una de sus principales fortalezas. Joey Ortiz se ha consolidado como una pieza importante para Milwaukee, aunque sus números ofensivos han bajado durante la postemporada.

Mujer pide 10 mdd a Yankees de Nueva York de la MLB tras ser golpeada por bate
El jugador también habló sobre Jonathan Aranda, su rival en la Serie Mundial. Joey Ortiz destacó el nivel del primera base de Tampa Bay y se refirió a la oportunidad de competir contra él en el Clásico de Otoño.
JoJo Romero es un lanzador zurdo nacido en Camarillo, California. El relevista llegó a los Brewers en agosto de 2026, después de jugar con los St. Louis Cardinals.
⚽ Mundial 2026
El resumen del Mundial en tu correo a las 7:00 am
Los partidos, las claves del día y el periódico para hojear — todo en un correo, todos los días. Gratis, y te das de baja con un clic.
Su función es trabajar desde el bullpen en momentos importantes de los partidos. Durante la postemporada, JoJo Romero ha tenido la responsabilidad de frenar a los bateadores rivales en las entradas finales.
Además, JoJo Romero formó parte de la selección mexicana en el Clásico Mundial de Beisbol. El lanzador explicó que sus abuelos siguen sus partidos por televisión y están pendientes de su trayectoria profesional.
Jonathan Aranda, otro de los mexicanos en MLB
Jonathan Aranda integra la lista de mexicanos que participan en la Serie Mundial 2026. El primera base nació en Tijuana y terminó la temporada regular con un promedio de bateo de .274, 22 jonrones y 92 carreras impulsadas.
En el primer partido de la final, Jonathan Aranda conectó tres imparables en tres turnos, recibió una base por bolas y anotó una carrera. Sin embargo, los Rays perdieron por 3-2 ante Milwaukee.
Manuel Rodríguez, nacido en Mérida, Yucatán, también busca un lugar en el Clásico de Otoño. El relevista derecho disputó seis partidos en la temporada regular, en los que registró una efectividad de 2.70 y sumó 10 ponches en seis entradas y dos tercios.
Así, los mexicanos afrontan la Serie Mundial con objetivos distintos. Joey Ortiz y JoJo Romero buscan conquistar el primer campeonato de los Brewers, mientras Jonathan Aranda intenta ayudar a Tampa Bay a levantar el título de las Grandes Ligas.

item.dc:creator: Dibyendu Mondal
item.description: Former Toronto Blue Jays pitcher Kevin Gausman was rumored to return in free agency. He was traded to the Chicago Cubs on Aug. 2. item.content:encoded:
Former Toronto Blue Jays pitcher Kevin Gausman was rumored to return in free agency. He was traded to the Chicago Cubs on Aug. 2.
Toronto received outfielder Brett Bateman and infielder Ty Southisene. Gausman was in the final year of a five-year, $110 million contract.
Now that the regular season has ended, rumors started swirling about a potential Gausman return due to his personal connection with the team and the city. He helped the Blue Jays reach the World Series last year. He went 5-10 with a 4.38 ERA in 23 starts for Toronto in 2026.
But despite Gausman’s wishes, the team does not plan on that, which has now forced the 35-year-old to move on as well.
Kevin Gausman’s $7.6 Million News Emerges
Gausman has put his Toronto home on the market this week with Harvey Kalles Real Estate for $6.885 million.
He bought the property in March 2022 for $7.65 million. The asking price sits $765,000 below that figure.
The house sits in Lytton Park, a Toronto neighborhood. It has six bedrooms, seven bathrooms and nearly 5,000 square feet, Blue Jays Insider reported. It was built in 2019.
The listing highlights a chef’s kitchen, a family room, a heated driveway and a south-facing backyard. The primary bedroom has a five-piece en suite bathroom and a walk-in closet. The family lived there for about four and a half years.
Gausman had not listed the house in the weeks after the trade. Reports in early October pointed to that as a possible sign of a return. The Athletic reported that a reunion with Toronto seemed likely if Gausman keeps playing.
Before the trade, Gausman told Sportsnet the family would leave Toronto after 2026. He was already preparing for a future out of the city.
Kevin Gausman Has Spoken Warmly About Toronto Since the Trade
Gausman said on the Baseball Isn’t Boring podcast that Toronto “was my second home.” He added that the family had a home there and that leaving was hard.
After his last Blue Jays start on Aug. 1, Gausman called signing with Toronto the best decision he ever made.
His wife, Taylor, wrote on Instagram on Aug. 3 that choosing Toronto was the family’s best decision. She wrote that the couple’s daughters grew up there. She declined to say goodbye and offered a see-you-later instead.
In March, Gausman said his family loved the city’s parks, its summers and its people. He said they also loved their house and neighborhood.
As he left the clubhouse after the trade, Gausman recalled his younger daughter’s first birthday party in the backyard. He also recalled a photo of both girls on the front step the week the family bought the house.
Gausman has said he hopes to show his daughters around Canada after he retires. He also wants to take them to Blue Jays games, MLB Trade Rumors reported. He said on the 6ix Inning Stretch podcast that he plans to return to Toronto after retiring.

item.title: [FanSided] How Jacob Misiorowski was almost a Rays ace, flipping the World Series upside down
item.dc:creator: Jake Elman
item.description: At some point during Friday’s World Series opener, we’re sure plenty of Tampa Bay Rays fans wished they had their own version of Jacob Misiorowski. As it turns out, the Rays may have been among those legitimately interested in having the real thing. item.content:encoded:
At some point during Friday’s World Series opener, we’re sure plenty of Tampa Bay Rays fans wished they had their own version of Jacob Misiorowski.
As it turns out, the Rays may have been among those legitimately interested in having the real thing.
Social media is far more efficient than people give it credit for, and a July 2025 article regarding the Brewers’ ace resurfaced on Friday morning. Major League Baseball’s Adam McCalvy reported last year that the Rays, Brewers and Rockies were the only three MLB teams that attended a December 2019 bullpen session in Kansas City to see the Miz, who at that point was in his senior year of high school and far lighter than his current 6-foot-7, 201-pound frame.
“I don’t know if I’ve ever written a report on a guy off one bullpen with that conviction,” Brewers regional scouting supervisor Drew Anderson said.
Misiorowski lost his senior season to the pandemic and enrolled at Crowder College (Mo.) after going undrafted. Milwaukee instead used a second-round pick on the future All-Star in 2022 — two spots ahead of Tampa, who took outfielder Brock Jones instead.
What would have happened had the Tampa Bay Rays drafted Jacob Misiorowski?
Whether it’s JaMarcus Russell or Greg Oden, sports fans love a good “what if?” discussion. We’re too early in Misiorowski’s career to fully evaluate and predict a world in which he landed in Tampa Bay instead of Milwaukee.
What we found interesting is that some in the Brewers’ 2020 draft room fought for Misiorowski and suggested paying him third-round money. But because the pandemic shortened the draft to five rounds, they felt they shouldn’t take the risk — which, for the record, we agree was the right call given the context.
But should the Rays have possibly taken the opposite approach and selected Misiorowski in 2020? Those questions are notoriously difficult in baseball; it’s easy to forget he was an 18-year-old who hadn’t pitched a meaningful game in over a year. We don’t know how he’d have fared without three years of experience — albeit temporarily halted by a freshman-year knee injury — in college and summer ball.
Anderson referenced Pirates ace Paul Skenes, who went No. 1 in 2023, and how easy a decision that was for Pittsburgh. Milwaukee lucked out, so to speak, by having an incredible player development program that consistently churns out above-average position players and reliable pitchers. Imagine if Misiorowski landed in Colorado?
Misiorowski did his part on Friday night, limiting the Rays to one run over five innings. Assuming the Brewers hold on and win their first World Series title, we hope Anderson and area scout Riley Bandelow receive better treatment than the New York Knicks’ employees.

item.content:encoded:
The Milwaukee Brewers won Game 1 of the World Series behind a solid start from Jacob Misiorowski. He went five innings and picked up the win.
It was Misiorowski's longest start of the postseason, and he was the Brewers' first starting pitcher to get a win in the postseason. The 24-year-old is poised to win the National League Cy Young Award in the coming weeks, and on Friday, he became the youngest starting pitcher since Jaret Wright to get a win in Game 1 of the World Series.
Wright's win came in 1997 when Cleveland played the Florida Marlins. He was 21 years old at the time.
It really puts into perspective how hard it is to pitch well on the biggest stage as a young pitcher. Misiorowski has been lighting up the radar gun this October, but he has been nowhere near as dominant as he was in the regular season.
The Brewers threw their best arm in Game 1, but the Tampa Bay Rays did not. Misiorowski will be lined up to pitch in Game 5, while Drew Rasmussen looks like he will pitch in Game 2 and Game 6, should the series get there.
However,. depending on how the series goes, the Brewers and Rays could both move where their aces are slated to pitch.

Uno de los protagonistas fue William Contreras el careta dejó una actuación histórica para un clásico de octubre. Contreras fue uno de los jugadores más destacados del encuentro brillando tanto con el madero, el ABS y desde la receptoría donde puso a dos corredores out en intento de robo para convertirse en el primer careta en la historia de la Serie
item.content:encoded:
Este viernes arrancó la Serie Mundial entre Tampa Bay y Cerveceros de Milwaukee quienes se llevaron el primer triunfo 3-2 gracias al poder criollo. Uno de los protagonistas fue William Contreras el careta dejó una actuación histórica para un clásico de octubre.
Contreras fue uno de los jugadores más destacados del encuentro brillando tanto con el madero, el ABS y desde la receptoría donde puso a dos corredores out en intento de robo para convertirse en el primer careta en la historia de la Serie Mundial en hacerlo.
Tras el encuentro y con Miguel Rojas, jugador recién retirado y ganador de dos anillos de Serie Mundial con Los Dodgers, como el entrevistador, Contreras regaló sus impresiones y destacó el buen trabajo del equipo sobre todo del bullpen. «Soy un jugador al que le gusta jugar con mucha pasión y mucha energía, y eso es lo que voy a hacer».
El jugador quien ha tenido una temporada de ensueño tras ganar el Clásico Mundial de Beisbol con Venezuela, también expresó que solo hace su trabajo desde la receptoría tratando siempre de estar en sintonía con el lanzador.
“Es mi manera de transmitirles confianza y darles ese impulso o empujón que necesitan cada vez que están en el montículo (…) No estoy seguro de cómo lo toman algunos de los muchachos, pero para mí eso era una prioridad”.
Lee también: Criollos sueñan con el doble campeonato en este 2026
Para finalizar el oriundo de Puerto Cabello también aseguró que con el sistemas de bolas y strikes es una lotería y que actualmente el se encuentra en un buen momento.
«En cuanto al ABS, estoy pasando por un buen momento, y creo que el ABS es algo parecido a batear en una temporada (…) Puedes pasar por una mala racha. Ahora mismo, creo que estoy pasando por un buen momento con él, y tengo que aprovecharlo», dijo.

item.title: [numerama.com] Avengers : Doomsday dévoile des images inédites (avec deux Captain America)

item.description: Marvel Studios a trouvé un endroit inattendu pour montrer de nouvelles images d’Avengers : Doomsday : une coupure publicitaire des World Series, la finale du championnat nord-américain de baseball. item.content:encoded:
Marvel Studios a trouvé un endroit inattendu pour montrer de nouvelles images d’Avengers : Doomsday : une coupure publicitaire des World Series, la finale du championnat nord-américain de baseball. Le spot est passé sur Fox ce vendredi 23 octobre, pendant le premier match entre les Brewers de Milwaukee et les Rays de Tampa Bay. En France, c’était dans la nuit de vendredi à samedi.
Pour les fans, ces images arrivent à moins de deux mois de la sortie, prévue le mercredi 16 décembre 2026 en France, deux jours avant les États-Unis. Elles s’ajoutent à la première bande-annonce, publiée le 20 juillet, et à la deuxième, dévoilée en août à la D23, la convention de fans de Disney. En revanche, elles ne révèlent rien de majeur sur l’intrigue.
Que montre le nouveau teaser d’Avengers : Doomsday ?
Ce spot joue à fond la carte du baseball. On retrouve les Quatre Fantastiques à Ebbets Field, l’ancien stade des Dodgers de Brooklyn, démoli en 1960 dans notre monde mais toujours debout dans le film.
Reed Richards (Pedro Pascal) y utilise son bras élastique pour lancer la première balle du match (c’est de la triche, non ?). Cinq joueurs de la MLB, la ligue nord-américaine de baseball, s’invitent aussi sur le banc : Bryce Harper (Phillies), Freddie Freeman (Dodgers), Randy Arozarena (Mariners), Junior Caminero (Rays) et Jacob Misiorowski, lanceur partant des Brewers pendant ce même premier match. Selon la MLB, la scène est bien tirée du film, mais les joueurs y ont été ajoutés pour ce spot.
Au milieu de ces images, Marvel s’amuse surtout de la présence de ses deux Captain America. Scott Lang, alias Ant-Man (Paul Rudd), appelle spontanément Steve Rogers (Chris Evans) « Cap », avant de se reprendre : le titre revient désormais à Sam Wilson (Anthony Mackie). Cette petite hésitation donne un aperçu des échanges que pourrait provoquer le retour de Steve, qui avait transmis son bouclier à Sam à la fin d’Avengers : Endgame.
Thor et Black Panther apparaissent également, tandis que Doctor Doom clôt la vidéo, toujours dissimulé sous son masque et sa capuche. Marvel montre ainsi ses héros et son méchant, sans rien dévoiler de ce qui les attend.

item.title: [trentonian.com] World Series: Brewers withstand Rays’ comeback attempt to win Game 1
item.dc:creator: Steve Megargee

item.content:encoded:
MILWAUKEE (AP) — Trevor Megill was shouting in celebration and the Milwaukee Brewers were bolting out of the dugout to congratulate one another, believing they had just escaped a ninth-inning jam to win Game 1 of the World Series.
Not quite yet.
What initially was ruled a game-ending double play got overturned after a video review showed Brewers shortstop Cooper Pratt’s right foot was slightly off the bag when he reached to catch a high throw from second baseman Brice Turang.
No problem.
Megill regrouped and struck out Jonny DeLuca with two runners in scoring position as Milwaukee edged the Tampa Bay Rays 3-2 on Friday night.
“It’s good to get the first win out of the way,” Megill said. “That’s where all the nerves are at. First game, a lot of anticipation and build-up to where we are right now.”
The ninth inning was particularly nerve-racking for the Brewers and the sellout crowd attending Milwaukee’s first World Series game since 1982.
“You have a big range of emotions,” said team captain Christian Yelich, whose RBI triple in the first put the Brewers ahead for good. “It’s a big credit to Trev for locking back in right there and making some huge pitches after you have that emotional dump and then have to get back on it.”
Tampa Bay trailed 3-1 and hadn’t put a runner on since the sixth until it mounted its comeback attempt against Megill.
Jonathan Aranda, who went 3 for 3 with a walk, and Chandler Simpson hit consecutive one-out singles. A double steal involving pinch-runner Jorge Mateo and Simpson put runners on second and third before Junior Caminero walked on a 3-2 pitch in the dirt to load the bases.
Liam Hicks hit a grounder to the right side, and Turang ranged well to his left to field the ball before throwing to Pratt to start what initially was called a 4-6-3 double play.
Fireworks went off, players poured onto the field and Milwaukee fans roared. But then the crowd hushed as it watched the play again on the videoboard.
“You’ve got to think worst-case scenario there,” Megill said. “I thought the challenge was at first base, maybe a bobble or something. But it was pretty clear once the replay went up that it was on the play at second base. Zoomed in and it didn’t look good. It’s all right. We picked up Cooper there. He’ll pick us up tomorrow.”
The out call at second was changed to safe by umpire Alfonso Márquez at the MLB Replay Center, which caught Pratt by surprise.
“Obviously, it was close,” the 22-year-old rookie said. “I just didn’t think it was enough to overturn, so I wasn’t thinking anything of it. The video I saw, thought my cleat was dragging. … There must have been some other angles that I haven’t seen. It ultimately didn’t matter because we won.”
The Brewers won because Megill got DeLuca to swing and miss at a 2-2 pitch, capping a night in which Tampa Bay went 0 for 6 with runners in scoring position.
“This is an extremely confident group,” Rays manager Kevin Cash said. “You know that. We know that. They’re going to be fine. I think the frustration comes from we were one swing of the bat away right at the end of potentially taking the lead.”
The Game 1 winner has gone on to win the World Series 62.8% of the time.
This marks the first World Series featuring two teams seeking their first championship since 1980, when the Philadelphia Phillies beat the Kansas City Royals in six games. The only other major league clubs without a World Series title are the Colorado Rockies, San Diego Padres and Seattle Mariners.
Milwaukee took a 2-0 lead in the first inning against Nick Martinez. NL Cy Young Award favorite Jacob Misiorowski allowed one run and four hits over five innings to help the Brewers stay in front before relievers Abner Uribe and Aaron Ashby shut down the Rays through the eighth.
Misiorowski, who had a season-low three strikeouts, opened the game with a 103.5 mph fastball — the fastest pitch ever thrown in a World Series.
“The adrenaline kind of took over, and I tensed up and threw it hard,” said Misiorowski, who earned the win. “Then I settled down, and that was the game plan, to settle in and do me. Don’t try and overdo it.”
Milwaukee’s Jackson Chourio and William Contreras each had two hits, including an RBI single. Contreras also threw out two runners trying to steal.
Tampa Bay managed to hang around thanks in part to Martinez, who gave up those two runs in the first but held Milwaukee scoreless through the rest of his five-inning stint. The Brewers added an insurance run in the seventh when Chourio singled home Pratt.
Then came all the action in the ninth, with the Brewers’ premature celebration followed by a team-wide sigh of relief as Pratt offered some parting words to Megill.
“I just said, ‘Thank you, man. Thanks for picking me up,’” Pratt said. “That’s what this game is. It’s a game of pick-me-up. He picked me up today.”
Up next
Drew Rasmussen (16-5, 2.67 ERA) pitches for Tampa Bay and Logan Henderson (11-3, 2.47) starts for Milwaukee in Game 2 on Saturday night. In this postseason, Rasmussen is 2-0 with a 1.29 ERA and Henderson is 0-0 with a 3.00 ERA.

item.content:encoded:
今季終了後にカブスからフリーエージェントとなった鈴木誠也外野手が、守備でも高い評価を受けた。米スポーツデータ会社『Sports Info Solutions（SIS）』が22日（日本時間23日）に発表した「フィールディング・バイブル賞」で、右翼手部門の3位にランクインした。
■守備指標が大幅改善
地元メディアも高評価
同賞は2006年に創設され、各守備位置の最優秀選手を選出。統計分析や目視評価などを基に、専門家らが投票する。今季の右翼手部門はウィルヤー・アブレイユ外野手（レッドソックス）が81ポイント、コービン・キャロル外野手（ダイヤモンドバックス）が53ポイントで1、2位となり、鈴木は43ポイントで3位にランクインした。
今季の鈴木は右翼手として111試合、972.2イニングに出場。MLB公式のデータサイト『Baseball Savant』によるOAA（Outs Above Average）が右翼手全体5位のプラス5を記録。一昨年のマイナス3、昨年のプラスマイナス0から大きく改善し、肩の強さと送球面での指標も優れていた。
今季は打撃だけでなく守備でも評価を高め、ゴールドグラブ賞の最終候補にも選出された。各球団の注目度は高く、人気銘柄の一人に挙がっている。

item.content:encoded:
MILWAUKEE – Jacob Misiorowski stepped on the mound for a World Series debut like no other.
“I had so much adrenaline built up,” he said.
Recommended Videos
He threw a pitch the likes of which had never been seen in the Fall Classic.
The Miz broke the World Series velocity record with his very first delivery, a 103.5 mph fastball to the Tampa Bay Rays’ Yandy Díaz that was taken high out of the strike zone for a ball. He allowed one run over five innings to get his first postseason win as a starter, helping the Milwaukee Brewers to a 3-2 victory in Friday night’s opener.
“I don’t even know how to tell you how I felt,” the 24-year-old right-hander said a half-hour after the end of a crazy ninth inning, prolonged by a game-extending video review. “I still don’t know how I felt. I feel like I’m still trying to take everything in and understand what happened.”
Misiorowski gave up four hits and one walk, striking out a season-low three.
Aroldis Chapman of the Chicago Cubs had the previous mark for fastest Series pitch at 103.2 mph in the ninth inning of Game 2 in 2016, an offering that resulted in a groundout to second by Cleveland’s Coco Crisp. The previous high by a Series starting pitcher since tracking began in 2008 was 101.1 mph by the New York Mets’ Noah Syndergaard to Kansas City’s Ben Zobrist that was taken for a ball in the first inning of Game 3 in 2015.
Miz reached 100 mph with 38 pitches, topping the previous Series high of 24 by Chapman in Game 5 of 2016. The most by a starting pitcher in the Series had been six by Tampa Bay’s Tyler Glasnow in the 2020 opener against the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Tampa Bay scored in the fourth when Jonathan Aranda walked, took third on Junior Caminero’s double over center fielder Garrett Mitchell and came around on Liam Hicks’ grounder to first baseman Jake Bauers.
Nearing the end of his first full major league season, Misiorowski has reached 100 mph with 134 of 260 postseason pitches. But his spin rate was down, a sign of a season in which he has pitched 188 innings — up from 141 1/3 innings last year. And he got just seven swings and misses, five on his fastball.
Tampa Bay batters fouled off 20 of his 78 pitches and tipped another.
During the regular season, Misiorowski reached 100 mph with 1,115 pitches, including a high of 105.5 mph to the Chicago Cubs’ Pete Crow-Armstrong on June 27.
“What we’re used to seeing in the regular season was Miz just mow through people and have two strikeouts an inning. That’s unrealistic,” Brewers manager Pat Murphy said. “This is the best team in the American League.”
Miz's first pitch was so fast the scoreboard at American Family Field couldn't keep up, flashing 103.4 mph — one-tenth of a mile less than it registered on MLB’s Statcast system.
“He’s such a special pitcher,” Rays manager Kevin Cash said. “I felt like for him to be out of the game at five innings, there’s a small win in that.”
Misiorowski threw fastballs on 10 of his first 12 pitches, then mixed in more offspeed stuff. In all he tossed 48 fastballs, 17 cutters, seven sliders and six curveballs.
Miz finished with 30 pitches at 101 mph or higher, 11 of 102 mph or more and three at 103-plus mph.
Warming up in the bullpen, he couldn't take in the introductions before Milwaukee's first World Series game in 44 years. He thought about how far he had come, how he was at Double-A Biloxi two years ago.
“It was crazy," he said. “It’s everything I dreamed of.”
___

item.content:encoded:
Brewers' Jacob Misiorowski drops brutally honest admission on his Game 1 start appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Milwaukee Brewers possessed a top-notch bullpen in the regular season and in the last two rounds of the playoffs, but the idea of this team winning a championship without Jacob Misiorowski posting his best stuff seemed near-incomprehensible. The presumptive National League Cy Young was unable to reach the sixth inning for a third straight postseason start, and yet, the Brew Crew are now just three wins away from capturing their first World Series title in franchise history.
Misiorowski pitched five innings of one-run ball in Friday's 3-2 Game 1 victory versus the Tampa Bay Rays, allowing four hits while recording three strikeouts and one walk. He perfectly described his fairly short yet triumphant outing.
"Not perfect, good enough to get a win," the genial 24-year-old right-hander said, via Joey Mistretta of ClutchPoints.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Misiorowski has not been operating as a work horse for some time. He has accumulated only a combined 13 1/3 innings of work across three playoff outings. The three Ks are also surprisingly low. This record-breaking flamethrower is nearing the end of his first full MLB campaign, and he is showing the effects of unleashing elite velocity all yearlong.
Like Misiorowski said, though, he had enough on this night. The Brewers' bullpen also provided first-class reinforcements, once again. Aaron Ashby remains unstoppable, Abner Uribe enjoyed a stellar showing in his own right and Trevor Megill survived despite allowing one run in the ninth. The lineup notched timely hits, as it does, and All-Star catcher William Contreras threw out potential game-tying runs multiple times.
Jacob Misiorowski did not carry the squad to a 1-0 series lead in American Family Field. Pat Murphy has not asked him to fill that role during this postseason. Milwaukee secured the W by putting forth a complete effort. This ballclub may not have many household names, but it should be obvious by now that one player does not define Brewers baseball.
If Milwaukee has its way, Misiorowski will not have to put the team on his back again for the rest of 2026. Game 2 is Saturday at approximately 8 p.m. ET.
Related: Brewers' Aaron Ashby reveals how he found his postseason groove in 2026
Related: Watch Brewers fans celebrate 1st World Series game win in 44 years

item.content:encoded:
La Serie Mundial 2026 apenas está por comenzar y el dominicano de los Rays, Junior Caminero, ya dio una muestra del poder que tiene en su madero al dañar la pantalla gigante del American Family Field, el estadio de los Brewers, donde se llevará a cabo el Juego 1 por el título de las Grandes Ligas de Béisbol (MLB).
El jueves por la noche, durante la práctica previa al primer desafío, Caminero conectó un batazo que fue a estrellarse contra la pantalla gigante; el panel de la jumbotron, que proyectaba el logo del Clásico de Otoño, quedó inservible por el resto de la práctica de bateo.
Junior Caminero's homer knocked out the lights on the American Family Field scoreboard ???? pic.twitter.com/pabSVoNloy
— MLB (@MLB) October 23, 2026
Caminero podría ser una de las piezas clave en el desarrollo de esta Serie Mundial, más aún llegando encendido tras su actuación en el Juego 6 de la Serie de Campeonato ante los Guardians, cuando disparó un jonrón contra el poste del jardín izquierdo durante la séptima entrada, produciendo las dos carreras que ampliaron definitivamente la delantera de los Rays.
Si la muestra del jueves por la noche es un anticipo de lo que puede hacer, Junior Caminero está listo para dejar su huella en esta Serie Mundial.

item.content:encoded:
If you expected the Milwaukee Brewers to enter the World Series without making any adjustments, you must not have been watching the team this season. Even after sweeping the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLCS and overcoming a red-hot Padres squad in the Division Series, manager Pat Murphy is always finding new ways to keep his opponents on their toes.
The Brewers released their batting order on Friday afternoon, just hours before first pitch. Their updated order will be as follows:
1. Jackson Chourio
2. Jake Bauers
3. Christian Yelich
4. William Contreras
5. Brice Turang
6. Garrett Mitchell
7. Cooper Pratt
8. Sal Frelick
9. David Hamilton
What should we take away from the Milwaukee Brewers' updated batting order for Game 1 of the World Series?
This new-look order should give the Brewers an interesting dynamic of staggering lefty and righty batters, likely in hopes of keeping Game 1 starter Nick Martinez, a righty, out of a consistent rhythm to begin the contest. By moving Contreras to fourth, it sets up Milwaukee's best home run hitter this postseason for a grand slam opportunity, should it arise. Meanwhile, Yelich at the third spot gives the Brew Crew a likely opportunity for some much-needed contact hitting early in the rotation.
It's far from surprising to see first baseman Jake Bauers taking such a firm position near the top of the batting order, as Bauers emerged as one of the most reliable offensive threats on the team, and frankly, in all of baseball. His ability to extend the pitch count and make contact persistently has been a thorn in the sides of pitchers everywhere, so this is likely Murphy's best attempt to extend Martinez's pitch count early.
Meanwhile, Turang slotting back into the fifth spot in the lineup makes sense given his inconsistent production thus far in the postseason. Through eight games, the 26-year-old is hitting just .222 with six hits to seven strikeouts. The good news, however, is that Turang turned a corner in the Dodgers series, logging hits in three of four hits, while scoring a run in each contest.
The end of the lineup should be of interest as well. All year long, Brewers fans grappled with questions over David Hamilton's place in the lineup, but through the postseason, he's certainly proving he belongs. Milwaukee is in serious need of some production late in the order, so all eyes will be on Hamilton, as well as Cooper Pratt and Sal Frelick, to carry that torch.
Overall, this is a wise move by Pat Murphy to make sure his lineup isn't identical to what Tampa Bay was expecting to see. Although the players are the same, a little shake-up in the order might force Martinez and the Rays' defense to think twice, which is all the Brewers can really ask for in a matchup of two teams that are this talented defensively.

item.content:encoded:
Jonathan Aranda has become a pivotal player for the Tampa Bay Rays.
By the end of the regular season, he had the second-most homers (22) in the franchise, behind Junior Caminero (42).
Before he enters the 2026 World Series, let’s learn five fast facts about his wife, who has watched him grow in his career.
1. They Got Married in 2025
On Oct. 24, 2025, the pair got married.
This means their first anniversary will take place during the World Series this year — a rare way to celebrate.
2. She Threw a Ceremonial First Pitch
On May 16, 2026, Milka threw the first pitch for Tampa Bay’s clash against the Miami Marlins at Tropicana Field.
Unfortunately, the Rays ended up facing a 10-5 loss to the Marlins that day, but they did end up winning the three-game series.
3. They Have a Daughter
Jonathan and Milka have a 2-year-old daughter named Regina.
Following her birth, he discussed how being a father has changed him.
“It’s definitely changed a little bit,” he said, per Adam Berry of MLB.com. “Now it’s a little easier because now I’m doing everything for her and our family.”
During that conversation, he also joked about having newfound “dad strength.”
4. Milka Is From Mexico
Not only is Jonathan from Mexico, but so is his wife.
Jonathan became the first Mexican-born first baseman, and they now proudly instill their culture in their daughter.
5. She Was With Jonathan Long Before He Exploded in the Big Leagues
Their early relationship was kept fairly quiet, but she has had the opportunity to watch him grow into the elite hitter he is today.
During the regular season, he slashed .274/.358/.434with a .792 OPS and a career-high 22 homers through 155 games.
Their marriage remains relatively private.
Where Do the Rays Stand Ahead of Game 1?
ST PETERSBURG, FLORIDA – SEPTEMBER 2: Jonathan Aranda #8 of the Tampa Bay Rays at bat in the bottom of the first inning against the New York Mets at Tropicana Field on September 2, 2026 in St Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images)
Tampa Bay enters the World Series as an underdog.
The Brewers appear to hold a slight edge over the Rays, but this isn’t shocking considering they led the majors 103-59 overall during the regular season.
Tampa Bay dominated during the ALDS and the ALCS, leading up to the moment they’ve been waiting for — a run in the Fall Classic.
KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI – JUNE 24: Manager Kevin Cash #16 of the Tampa Bay Rays talks with reporters prior to a game against the Kansas City Royals at Kauffman Stadium on June 24, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Ed Zurga/Getty Images)
There’s always a chance they could upset Milwaukee, but doing so will be on easy feat.

item.title: [Heavy.com] Paige Almendariz, Christian Yelich's Girlfriend: 5 Fast Facts You Need to Know
item.dc:creator: Cole Sullivan
item.description: The World Series will be historic no matter how it plays out, as neither the Milwaukee Brewers nor the Tampa Bay Rays have ever won a championship. While the series means a lot to everyone competing, it could be a special moment for former NL MVP Christian Yelich. Here are five interesting facts about their r
item.content:encoded:
The World Series will be historic no matter how it plays out, as neither the Milwaukee Brewers nor the Tampa Bay Rays have ever won a championship.
While the series means a lot to everyone competing, it could be a special moment for former NL MVP Christian Yelich. He’s in his 14th season and will have his first opportunity to play for a World Series title.
One of his biggest supporters over the next few weeks will be his girlfriend, Paige Almendariz.
Here are five interesting facts about their relationship together.
Who Is Almendariz?
Like Yelich, Almendariz is a professional athlete in her own right. She currently plays defender for DC Power in the USL Super League.
The 29-year-old was born and raised in Sacramento, California, and has developed into a successful soccer player. Throughout her career, she has also played for clubs in Portugal, including Benfica and Braga, and won multiple titles. Now, Yelich will try to add a championship of his own.
How Did Almendariz and Yelich First Meet?
The two have kept their relationship relatively private, but they reportedly began dating in late 2025 and made their romance public through social media.
Almendariz has continuously shared photos of herself, Yelich and her dog on several occasions.
Check it out:
They Are Both California Natives
As mentioned, Almendariz is from California, and so is Yelich. He was born and raised in Thousand Oaks and attended Thousand Oaks High School.
However, they grew up roughly 400 miles apart, with West Sacramento, where Almendariz grew up, about a seven-hour drive from Thousand Oaks.
Yelich graduated from high school in 2010, while Almendariz graduated in 2016.
They Were Both Division I College Athletes
Both were Division I athletes, although Yelich took a different path when it came to his college commitment.
Out of high school, he committed to play baseball at the University of Miami, a long way from California. However, after the Florida Marlins drafted him, he elected to sign with the MLB team and turn pro immediately. That decision ultimately worked out, given the career he’s had.
As for Almendariz, she enrolled at UNLV to play college soccer after graduating as the valedictorian of her class, staying relatively close to home.
She was a standout defender for the university from 2016 to 2019 before heading to Portugal in 2020 to sign with Lank Vilaverdense.
They Both Have Athletic Siblings
Athletics run in both families. Yelich’s younger brother, Collin, was drafted by the Atlanta Braves in 2015 and played professional baseball for several years, while his other brother, Cameron, served in the United States Marine Corps.
Almendariz is one of five sisters, and her sister Brittany also played Division I soccer at UNLV as a defender. The two even shared the field when Paige was a freshman.

item.content:encoded:
In the almost immediate aftermath of the Atlanta Braves being eliminated from the MLB playoffs, a report surfaced that Ronald Acuña Jr. had partnered with the predictions company Kalshi.
NYT Reporter Andrew Baggarly wrote (on 10/7):
"Atlanta Braves star outfielder Ronald Acuña Jr. has partnered with Kalshi, making him the first Major League Baseball player to venture into the potentially thorny area of prediction markets."
Amid the Braves being eliminated from the MLB playoffs, Acuña Jr. has since been under fire for a controversial social media post in which he is promoting the company, Kalshi.
More MLB on Heavy: Atlanta Braves 2-Year Pitcher Still a Free Agent 94 Days After Release
Ronald Acuña Jr. Sends Out Kalshi Promotion Post
Well, now that Ronald Acuña Jr. is partnered with Kalshi, he has to promote the company, right?
He did just that with the following post:
It's a 30-second-long video with a Kalshi tag and shoutout at the end.
Since being posted on Thursday (10/22) evening, the message has garnered over 540K views, 1.3K likes, and 100+ comments.
Here are some notable comments of being expressing their displeasure/frustration:
@kirbyssmart: "Gambling has infected everything I love"
@AdrianLaFosse: "Love ya, dude, but taking Kalshi money is sad. The world has a gambling problem, and now it is a push away on their phone."
@hesipsgreen: "this video is .30 seconds long and you hit .133 in the playoffs vs the dodgers!"
Kalshi likely opened up the checkbook to get a partnership with Acuña Jr., and sometimes it's hard to fault athletes for taking on these partnerships when it's such an easy payday.
@og_yungdilly: "Listen I gamble dang near everyday nothing crazy But even im getting tired of all these ads man like how much are they paying u for this"
@justincamblin: "Disappointed you're promoting gambling. This stuff will ruin sports and people's lives."

item.content:encoded:
Mets still have serious first base problem after Pete Alonso signed with Orioles originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
Last offseason, the New York Mets opted not to re-sign Pete Alonso, as the first baseman signed with the Baltimore Orioles.
It's safe to say the Mets probably regret that decision, as their offense could've used the 43 home runs and 113 RBIs Alonso produced in 2026.
Jorge Polanco, Alonso's replacement, played just 37 games and had -1.4 bWAR before season-ending ankle surgery in August.
For the Mets to achieve an "A+" offseason, they must address their first base problem, FanSided's Zachary Rotman wrote.
"Letting Pete Alonso walk in free agency was a decision that made sense given how power-hitting first basemen over 30 tend to age historically, but it also required the Mets to find an adequate replacement.
"Given the fact that their first basemen ranked 29th in the Majors with an 85 wRC+ and dead last with -1.4 fWAR in 2026, it's clear that [David] Stearns did not do a good enough job in that area," Rotman wrote.
One player the Mets could target is Teruaki Sato, who won the Triple Crown in Nippon Professional Baseball.
The worst-case scenario is if the Mets have Jared Young as their everyday starter on Opening Day.
"Jared Young as a platoon option at first base is fine enough, but the Mets either need to acquire a good right-handed bat to pair with him against left-handed pitchers or acquire a legitimate every-day starter — whether that's Teruaki Sato in free agency or someone else via trade. It's hard to field a potent offense if you get nothing out of the first base position," Rotman added.
Given how poorly New York's first basemen hit in 2026, adding a veteran right-handed hitter or someone like Sato should be a top priority this offseason.

item.content:encoded:
Why Rays' key to World Series victory might revolve around Jacob Misiorowski originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Tampa Bay Rays are facing the Milwaukee Brewers in the 2026 MLB World Series, and after the Brewers swept the reining champions in four games in the NLCS, the Brewers are favorites in this matchup.
They also have home-field advantage, which makes the Rays' task a lot harder. But there's certainly a path for the Rays to win it all. But how can they actually win the World Series?
ESPN's Alden Gonzalez highlighted how the Brewers have a vulnerable starting rotation, led by Jacob Misiorowski, and that if the Rays can chase him out of the game early, the Rays could be set up for a lot of success in the World Series.
Rays can beat Brewers by getting after Jacob Misiorowski
"To beat the Brewers, you have to take advantage of their starting rotation," Gonzalez writes. "It begins with running up the pitch counts of their two front-line starters, Jacob Misiorowski and Logan Henderson."
If the Rays are able to make the Brewers' top-two starting pitchers throw a lot of pitches early in games, making it so they don't last long in their respective starts, they can have a real chance of winning it all.
It might seem like a simple thing to chase a pitcher early, but considering the Brewers' top-heavy bullpen, getting to the middle of the bullpen might prove to be a key to this series.
Besides, in Games 3 and 4, Milwaukee will be relying on more of their bullpen, with starters Dustin May, Shane Drohan, and Robert Gasser set to be involved.
If the Rays can force the Brewers to the bullpen early in Games 1 and 2, they could set themselves up nicely for the rest of the series.
As Gonzalez put it, "scoring early will be a must for the Rays." They can win the World Series even if they struggle against Misiorowski and Henderson, but if they have success against them, their odds of winning the series will increase significantly.
The snowball effect of chasing Misiorowski and/or Henderson from a game early would be huge. Taxing the Brewers' bullpen is the key to the Rays' success, and to do so, they're going to have to get after Misiorowski.
Games 1 and 2 might be a telling outcome for how the series will go. If the Rays can tax the bullpens, they could be set up for success once the series heads to Tampa Bay.
They'll need their own pitchers to play great, but if the Rays' offense can force the pitch counts of Henderson and Misiorowski to go high early in their respective starts, they could be set up for success in the World Series against the Brewers.

Goldschmidt could likely be signed to another one-year deal that would not lead to any risk for the Yankees.
He is a solid (and well liked) veteran who can still help the team compete for a World Series in 2027.

As someone who married into a family of Rays fans and will be in Florida with my wife’s family for Halloween I would love to say the Rays will win in seven and I will watch that game with her family, but it is hard to vote against the Brewers. They have the bette
item.content:encoded:
Another season is coming to a close – the World Series is here. The Milwaukee Brewers and the Tampa Bay Rays, both vying for their first championship. Who do we think will win? In how many games? Who will get MVP? Here are our thoughts.
As someone who married into a family of Rays fans and will be in Florida with my wife’s family for Halloween I would love to say the Rays will win in seven and I will watch that game with her family, but it is hard to vote against the Brewers.
They have the better offense. They have the better starting pitching. They have the deeper bullpen. They may even be better defensively. And they are going to be a bit more rested.
Because I will be on an airplane for game six I will say that the Brewers will win in six games.
The fun WSMVP choice would be Aaron Ashby continuing to dominate and taking the award by storm but a reliever has not won the WSMVP since Mariano Rivera in 1999 and Ashby is not the team’s primary closer.
So I will go with Jacob Misiorowski throwing two elite starts in games one and five, as well as an impact relief appearance in game six.
I think these teams are pretty evenly matched – the Rays have the upper hand in starting pitching, the Brewers have the better bullpen. While the Brewers scored more runs in the regular season, the teams had similar rate stats (Milwaukee had a 105 OPS+, compared to Tampa Bay’s 103). The Rays’ starters have consistently worked deeper into games compared to Milwaukee, and I wonder at what point the wear and tear will start to get to the Brewers’ bullpen. The Rays don’t strike out often, which leads me to believe they can be the team that finally conquers Milwaukee’s relievers. Milwaukee’s offense was relentless against the Dodgers, so it won’t be easy for the Rays to keep the Brewers down.
Overall, I think this will be a hard-fought series, with the Rays emerging victorious in seven games. Drew Rasmussen will win World Series MVP, winning his starts in Game 1 and Game 5, then coming out of the bullpen to pitch in Game 7.
Brewers in 7, Jackson Chourio is MVP. I wish Bob Uecker was here to see it.
Brewers in six. This should be a really fun and competitive series between two teams who play baseball the right way. Pitching wins, especially in the postseason, so Jacob Misiorowski will win the MVP after authoring his postseason legacy with two elite starts and a gutsy appearance out of the bullpen with everything on the line.
Brewers in 6. Christian Yelich wins MVP as he lives up to his newly minted captain status. Tampa will give them a run for their money!
Rays in 7. Freddy Peralta World Series MVP, because why not. He enters in desperation relief to get the final out.

item.content:encoded:
There were 13 outfield-eligible players worth at least $20 in the FanGraphs Player Rater in 2026, just two fewer than the first base spot. If you remember that you only need to start one first baseman (and potentially a corner infielder and DH) while you might need to start as many as five outfielders at a time, well, you can see why this is problematic.
That's not to say the outfield is somehow a wasteland for Fantasy right now. First base was unusually strong in 2026, but in 2025, there were three times as many $20 players with outfield eligibility as at first base. And it's worth noting that the 13 $20 outfielders in 2026 are actually a few more than 2025's nine.
On the whole, I look at outfield as a position with a decent amount of depth in a three-outfielder, 12-team league. You should be able to draft a full lineup without feeling too bad about your outfield options in that formula.
Once you start getting into five-outfielder leagues, and especially deeper leagues with 15 teams, it starts to feel a lot more thin. That's to be expected, of course, but it's important to keep that in mind when you're preparing for the 2027 season. You don't have to make the position a priority in every draft, but if you aren't cognizant of it, you could end up with a real weakness in those deeper leagues.
For more on the state of the outfield position, .
2026 Outfield Review
- Pete Crow-Armstrong, CHC: .280 - 119 - 45 - 107 - 41
- Yordan Alvarez, HOU: .316 - 105 - 42 - 106 - 1
- Fernando Tatis Jr., SDP: .289 - 96 - 25 - 83 - 38
- Randy Arozarena, SEA: .281 - 113 - 26 - 79 - 26
- Jordan Walker, STL: .269 - 97 - 29 - 102 - 22
- James Wood, WSN: .265 - 106 - 30 - 77 - 21
- Jackson Chourio, MIL: .291 - 96 - 25 - 75 - 23
- Alec Burleson, STL: .279 - 89 - 26 - 116 - 4
- Jake McCarthy, COL: .291 - 80 - 15 - 83 - 32
- Michael Harris II, ATL: .294 - 79 - 26 - 87 - 12
- Jackson Merrill, SDP: .254 - 86 - 26 - 87 - 27
- Bryce Harper, PHI: .269 - 93 - 29 - 87 - 7
- Jake Bauers, MIL: .266 - 93 - 26 - 86 - 11
- Seiya Suzuki, CHC: .270 - 96 - 26 - 86 - 3
- Carson Benge, NYM: .282 - 86 - 20 - 65 - 22
- Andy Pages, LAD: .274 - 75 - 23 - 85 - 13
- Corbin Carroll, ARI: .239 - 91 - 22 - 78 - 21
- Oneil Cruz, PIT: .280 - 65 - 20 - 67 - 30
- Daylen Lile, WSN: .246 - 81 - 22 - 89 - 15
- Jac Caglianone, KCR: .289 - 72 - 23 - 75 - 7
- Bryan Reynolds, PIT: .261 - 102 - 17 - 72 - 9
- Chandler Simpson, TBR: .306 - 66 - 0 - 38 - 46
- Riley Greene, DET: .280 - 79 - 21 - 75 - 3
- Ceddanne Rafaela, BOS: .285 - 67 - 16 - 70 - 17
"Marginal player signs with the Rockies and has a Coors Field-inflated career season" used to be a pretty reliable archetype. Still, the Rockies have given Fantasy players little to get excited about in recent years. Jake McCarthy stands out as a notable exception, as his contact-and-speed profile proved to be a perfect fit for Coos Field. We're talking about relatively easy career-best production across the board, in a way that feels relatively obvious in retrospect. I don't have a ton of faith that this would prove replicable in any other ballpark — the gap between his .321 expected wOBA and his .349 actual mark was the 20th biggest in baseball — but it works there. As long as he isn't traded, McCarthy is a good bet to replicate his 2026 success.
I also want to highlight Harris and Merrill, because it feels very natural to group them together. They're both younger than you might realize – Harris will turn 26 shortly before his sixth MLB season in March, while Merrill won't even be 24 on Opening Day. They're also both linked by the combination of plus athleticism and bat speed, plus pretty poor approaches at the plate. They are, on the whole, capable of overcoming their poor swing decisions with outlier outcomes when they make contact, but that isn't always the case for either. Hence, the lengthy slumps that have held both back in recent years. They both got the good end of their range of outcomes in 2026, and we saw how high the ceiling can be for both. But drafting either for their 2026 outcome will carry inherent risks until they show some growth in their plate discipline.
Biggest Breakout from 2026
Pete Crow-Armstrong, Cubs
How could it be anyone else? Crow-Armstrong went from being a talented but deeply flawed hitter to arguably the best player in baseball, and he did it in-season. Early on, he looked more or less like the same guy he had always been, walking just nine times in 128 plate appearances through the end of June; he walked at least 12 times in each of the final five months of the season, something he had never done in any of his previous 13 months. He did that without sacrificing the pull-side power that has long been a key part of his game, and it turned him into one of the most dominant hitters in the game. Expecting all of those gains to carry over into 2027 might be asking a bit much — sometimes guys just get super locked in for a while — but he's clearly a much-improved hitter, and one who should be the first player taken in every single Roto league in 2027. And he shouldn't go much later in points leagues, where he was also the top player in 2026.
Honorable Mention: Jordan Walker, Cardinals
Okay, so if it were going to be anyone but Crow-Armstrong, it would be Walker, who went from being one of the biggest prospect busts in recent seasons to one of the best players in Fantasy. Walker still had pretty bad plate discipline and swing-and-miss issues, but he overcame that by being more aggressive early in the count and by doing more damage when he did make contact. The plate discipline issues and a late-season swoon — his expected wOBA dropped from .374 to .290 from the first half to the second — hint at the kind of risk involved in buying fully into what he did in 2026, and I suspect I'll be a little lower on him than the consensus. On the other hand, those were the exact reasons I cited to avoid Crow-Armstrong before the season, and look how that turned out. There's something to be said for just betting on the young, super-talented players when they show it.
Biggest Bust from 2026
The overall numbers don't show it, but Judge looked more or less like himself before he started dealing with that rib injury. In March and April, he posted a .450 xwOBA, right in line with his typical mark, but then things went downhill even before he ultimately went on the IL with a fractured rib. Was his downturn because of the injury? If so, then I think you can still make the case for him as a top-five pick in any league. But we're talking about a guy who will be 35 early next season, coming off a largely lost season that also came with an apparent decline in the underlying skill level, and that's a lot of red flags to overlook in a top-five pick. I might end up with Judge ranked that way come the spring, but it won't feel good.
Honorable Mention: Kyle Tucker, Dodgers
Maybe you don't think he was worth the contract the Dodgers gave him. Fair enough; you won't be alone in holding that opinion. But anyone who tells you there was any way to see this kind of disaster coming from Tucker is just lying to you. A 29-year-old went out and posted the worst batting average, on-base percentage, and slugging percentage of his career, and in two of those cases, it wasn't even close. Tucker had the combination of bat speed, athleticism, and plate discipline that should protect him against this kind of drop-off. Maybe the lights in L.A. were too bright for him. Maybe the pressure of the contract got to him. But I don't believe Tucker has just completely lost the ability to be an impact player, and he's still in what should be one of the best lineups in baseball, so I'll buy the bounce-back at what should be a steeply discounted price. The fact that he put together an excellent September and a very good postseason run certainly makes that an easier story to tell, of course.
Biggest rankings movers from 2026 to 2027
Up: Pete Crow-Armstrong, Cubs; Yordan Alvarez, Astros; Jordan Walker, Cardinals; Jake Bauers, Brewers
As maybe the biggest Yordan Alvarez believer in the entire Fantasy industry coming into 2026, I do worry there's going to be a big overcorrection on him in 2027. We didn't learn anything new about Alvarez. If you think 2026 was a breakout season of some sort for him, I'm sorry, but you just weren't paying attention; he's just always been this good. His .442 xwOBA was higher than his career average, sure, but it was also not even the highest of his career, and he had a separate season with a .436 mark, too. The skills have always been there, but the difference is that he stayed healthy in 2026 after a bunch of injuries in previous seasons. I'm thrilled that he stayed healthy, and the fact that he did it in a season when his standing among Fantasy players was never lower is a good reminder that the Fantasy community isn't nearly as good at predicting who will and won't stay healthy as we think. But that will also be true in 2027: He'll be a top-five pick in most leagues despite the injury risk not being substantially different than it was last season. That's not to say he shouldn't be a top-five pick, of course; it's to say that he should have been a lot closer to a top-five pick last season than he was.
You could make a case for Bauers as the biggest breakout at outfield, because he was viewed as an even bigger afterthought than Walker was. He was a 30-year-old platoon specialist, after all! That he somehow went out in 2026 and put up a .901 OPS against lefties and had the best season of his career by a mile came completely out of nowhere, and it's going to be very interesting to see what the market for him as a free agent looks like this offseason. I buy a lot of what he did in 2026, and I suspect there will be enough skepticism around it to keep his price pretty reasonable. But betting on age-30 breakouts is historically a pretty bad idea, so you'll have to get a pretty big discount on what he did in 2026 to make him worth the risk, I think.
Down: Ronald Acuna, Braves; Kyle Tucker, Dodgers; Wyatt Langford, Rangers; Brent Rooker, Athletics
I wanted to make Langford one of the biggest bust picks, if only to highlight the fact that he has almost certainly been the least profitable pick in Fantasy over the past three years. He has struggled to stay healthy and just hasn't been the impact player you'd expect from a guy who had the kind of prospect pedigree he did — not to mention the benefit of the doubt the Fantasy community has continued to give him. I suspect that will come to an end in 2027, and … it kind of makes me more excited about buying into him this season. Because, for as frustrating and disappointing as he's been as a big-leaguer, his per-162 game pace for his career is pretty terrific: 90 runs, 24 homers, 24 steals, and 77 RBI. If he just does that in 2027, isn't that worth something like a fifth-round pick? And I don't think that's the ceiling for Langford, who has put up those numbers at a very young age while playing through a variety of injuries and has certainly flashed a higher ceiling at times. I'm not trying to excuse his poor performance; I'm just pointing out that all he has to do is stay healthy to be a very good Fantasy option. That's usually a good player to buy into at a discount.
The notoriously frugal A's are surely feeling some degree of buyer's remorse on Rooker's contract, but that contract should assure that he continues to play every day for them. His disappointing season came to an end after just 48 games, but he was on pace for another 30-homer season despite the injury. The .200 average is a tough look, as was the career-worst 32% strikeout rate, and the big drop off as a 31-year-old will rightly lead to plenty of skepticism around the potential of a bounce back. But that will also mean Rooker will come at a huge discount, potentially with a price outside the top 200 in many drafts. I'll buy that dip, personally. If you can buy him as a very cheap bench bat, there's no downside.
Offseason preview
Who needs an upgrade most?
A bunch of these teams are straddling the line between trying to go for it and needing to rebuild. The Reds could very well be in the market for a big upgrade in the outfield, or they could decide to move Elly De La Cruz and hit the reset button (again). The Astros could decide to give it one more run with this core, or they could move Alvarez and pivot to the future. The Phillies seem most likely to try to take a big swing, if only because Dave Dombrowski only knows how to take big swings. However, the Cardinals loom as a team that is ascending and could decide to get involved in the free-agent market with their core of cost-controlled position players.
Top impending free agents
- Randy Arozarena
- Seiya Suzuki
- Ian Happ
- Jake Bauers
- Trent Grisham
- Daulton Varsho
- Luis Robert
- Ramon Laureano
- George Springer
Arozarena is such a fascinating free agent. He's coming off a perfectly timed career-best season, but he'll be 32 before Opening Day and has rated out as a pretty terrible defender for several years running. There's probably no chance he gets anything more than a five-year contract in free agency, and he might need to agree to a move to DH as soon as 2027, two things that might be a tough pill to swallow. But having the best season of his career in the toughest offensive environment in baseball is no small thing, and nobody can deny his flair for the dramatic would be a great fit for a team with championship aspirations. The underlying skill set doesn't look so different from previous seasons, but his price will likely be higher than ever, making him one of the more obvious players to avoid in drafts for 2027, no matter where he lands.
Suzuki and, to a lesser extent, Happ look like players who will carry pretty solid value in Fantasy no matter where they land, but everyone else looks pretty context-dependent. Varsho's pull-heavy swing (and elite center field defense) would be a perfect fit for the Yankees, for example, but would be a much less interesting profile elsewhere. Stay tuned.
Trade candidates 
- Yordan Alvarez, Astros
- Jarren Duran, Red Sox
- Steven Kwan, Guardians
- Byron Buxton, Twins
- Brent Rooker, Athletics
- Jake McCarthy, Rockies
Alvarez feels like the biggest wild card here. The Astros won the AL West, but with just a .500 record, and they had such a poor showing in a two-game Wild Card round loss to the White Sox that the hometown crowd showered them with boos along the way. The Astros have lost their long-held edge over the competition, and while Alvarez's contract isn't expiring, he only has two years left on a relatively below-market deal. So this might be their last chance to maximize their return for him. The Astros are in flux in a lot of ways after firing Dana Brown, so they might not be positioned to make a big, franchise-altering move, but they would probably be best served trying to get off the treadmill of mediocrity sooner rather than later.
It increasingly looks like the Red Sox should have traded Duran at least a year ago, if not longer. All of a sudden, he's a 30-year-old corner outfielder who probably shouldn't play every day against lefties, and while he'll likely still earn a below-market salary in arbitration, he no longer looks like a real bargain. His skill set still has plenty of value for Fantasy (20 homers, 21 steals will always play), and I'd bet on him improving on last year's .207 average, but this isn't an early-round profile anymore.
Top rookies to know for 2026
- Josue De Paula, Dodgers
- Walker Jenkins, Twins
- Eduardo Quintero, Dodgers
- Theo Gillen, Rays
- Mike Sirota, Dodgers
- Zyhir Hope, Tigers
- Edward Florentino, Pirates
- Eric Hartman, Braves
- Drew Burress, Athletics
- Josiah Hartshorn, Cubs
- Lazaro Montes, Mariners
Jenkins is probably the most likely player here to be in an Opening Day lineup – I'm not sure what would have to happen for him not to be there, absent injury. He didn't take the league by storm in his first 26 games, but he was actually pretty great once he got adjusted, hitting .385/.400/.615 with just three strikeouts over his final 10 games. He has power, speed, and an excellent approach at the plate and should be a popular breakout candidate for 2027.
But not as popular as De Paula could be. I say "could" because, well, there's no obvious place for him to play. It's definitely not going to be in right field or DH, and slotting De Paula in at left field would require finding somewhere for Teoscar Hernandez and his large salary to go. Center field is the biggest hole in the Yankees outfield, but De Paula hasn't played there since 2023, and … well, you see the problem here. De Paula destroyed Double-A and very much passed the eye test in 11 MLB games, earning not-totally-unfair comparisons to Juan Soto and Yordan Alvarez for his approach at the plate. He could be an absolute star, but given the roster crunch and the fact that he's only 21 and hasn't played at Triple-A yet, this might be a situation like Junior Caminero's a few years back – remember, he debuted toward the end of the 2023 season but wasn't an everyday player until August of 2024. I hope it doesn't take that long, but we'll have to at least consider the possibility that it will.

item.content:encoded:
Jacob Misiorowski is incredible, but meet Rays' Junior Caminero, who is the best in baseball at hitting a 100 MPH fastball originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
Looking at the World Series matchup, the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays have a great opportunity to win this.
The Brewers are a great team from top to bottom and don't make many mistakes, while the Rays keep winning with elite starting pitching, timely hitting, and a superstar in Junior Caminero.
Caminero might be one of the better players in Major League Baseball, but unfortunately, outside of fans who truly follow the game, he doesn't get as much hype as he deserves.
As weird as that might sound for a guy who hit 42 home runs this season and 45 last year, it feels like Caminero doesn't get the respect he deserves.
Misiorowski is well known, even to casual fans, because of how hard he throws. He's a guy who's going to consistently throw 100-plus miles per hour.
But here's the thing: Caminero is arguably the best hitter in Major League Baseball on high-velocity pitches. According to BaseballThings.com, he's hitting .358 with a ridiculous .580 OPS on pitches 96-plus miles per hour.
Baseball fans are in for a treat when these two meet, as Misiorowski will toe the rubber in Game 1.
They've gone at it before, and Misiorowski has struck Caminero out twice in three at-bats, with the Rays slugger failing to get a hit. Caminero keeps proving he can step up in big moments, so it wouldn't be surprising to see him get Misiorowski this time around.

item.content:encoded:
Brewers' Jacob Misiorowski set to make MLB World Series history two pitches into Game 1 originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays will meet for what's expected to be a very exciting World Series. In Game 1, we'll get to watch a guy like Jacob Misiorowski toe the rubber and throw at a level we haven't really seen before in this league, at least in the World Series.
Game 1 of the World Series won't make or break the series, but the Brewers and Rays have to feel that if they get off to a good start, they're in a better position than if they don't.
The Rays also have one of their big-time arms ready to go, with right-hander Nick Martinez expected to start Game 1.
It was surprising that Drew Rasmussen didn't get the ball, as Rasmussen is among the best starters in Major League Baseball and has been lights out all year, posting a 2.67 ERA in the regular season.
He's also been lights out in the postseason, posting a one-hit, eight-inning showing against the New York Yankees in the ALDS, plus two starts against the Cleveland Guardians in which he went at least 6.0 innings and allowed only one and two runs, respectively.
But for Misiorowski, there is more for all baseball fans to consider.
We'll get to see somebody make history, as his fastball is going to light up the radar gun. According to the latest, there's only been one pitch thrown by a starter in a World Series game at 101-plus miles per hour since 2008. Misiorowski is bound to change that in a major way.
"Only 1 pitch has been thrown by a starting pitcher in a World Series game at 101+ MPH in the entire pitch tracking era (2008-now).
"That is about to change," Codify Baseball wrote.
There's a very good chance we'll see 101-plus from Misiorowski throughout the game, and he'll probably have a couple of 103-pluses.
This is a guy who has a fastball that we've never seen before from a starting pitcher, and while some Major League Baseball fans might not love that it's two small-market teams going at it, we're going to see a boatload of talent, and he's one of the guys who's going to provide that.

item.content:encoded:
Brewers' Jacob Misiorowski ridiculously did something 89% of the time with 102+ MPH fastball originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays will meet in the World Series, starting Friday night in what's expected to be one of the more exciting World Series we've seen in quite some time.
Based on talent and other factors, both teams are equally matched, with small markets and young superstar talent.
For the Brewers, there might not be a bigger young superstar pitcher in Major League Baseball than Jacob Misiorowski. All Misiorowski has done this year is throw baseball at a ridiculous level, with the expectation that he'll win the National League Cy Young Award.
Misiorowski hasn't been bad by any means in the postseason, but also hasn't been great. He's thrown only 8.1 innings in his first two starts, with at least 88 pitches in each.
He still only allowed one earned run against the Los Angeles Dodgers and two against the San Diego Padres.
Misiorowski arguably has the best fastball in Major League Baseball, with some even thinking he has, or could have, the best in MLB history. As for what he's done this season, he's thrown more pitches at 102+ mph than nearly every other starter in baseball history, which is flat-out ridiculous.
"There have been 412 pitches thrown by MLB starters at 102+ MPH in the entire pitch tracking era and Jacob Misiorowski threw 365 of them this season. It's completely ridiculous," Codify Baseball wrote.
The biggest question Misiorowski will have to answer in the World Series is whether he can stay on the mound for six-plus innings.
Even during parts of the regular season, it wasn't exactly like this was a workhorse throwing complete games left and right. He hasn't thrown more than 6.1 innings in any start since Aug. 2, though multiple factors could explain it, as the Brewers arguably have the best bullpen in Major League Baseball and trust a lot of guys coming in during the back half of games.

item.title: [mlb.com] Our experts make their World Series predictions
item.dc:creator: Max Ralph
